roles.title: Role Permissions
roles.description: These permissions apply to members based on their role. Owner and Admin are unrestricted.

roles.adminDescription: Admins have full tool, Skill, Bash, and file permissions in the active workspace.

rolePermissions.title: Role Permissions
rolePermissions.description: These settings apply only to Normal members. Owners and Admins are unrestricted.
rolePermissions.skillAllowlistHint: One skill name per line. Only these skills can be invoked by Normal members.
rolePermissions.bashWhitelistHint: One command prefix per line. Normal members can only run commands that start with one of these prefixes.
rolePermissions.passlistHint: Commands on this list may run outside the sandbox without an approval round. Stored as structural rules and evaluated per subcommand, so compound commands cannot sneak past. Everything else that leaves the sandbox goes to approval or is denied.
rolePermissions.passlistEmpty: Empty is the correct default — nothing to configure. Everyday commands run inside the sandbox; out-of-sandbox requests go to approval or are denied.
rolePermissions.passlistPreviewPrefix: Matches any command starting with this prefix
rolePermissions.passlistCompositeRejected: Composite commands are not allowed here (|, &&, ;, $(), backticks). The rule engine already evaluates compound commands per subcommand — add only the single subcommand you want to allow.
rolePermissions.passlistDuplicate: This rule is already in the list.
rolePermissions.skillsHint: Which skills this bot offers — applies to every role. Unmounted skills are hidden from the model; disabled skills are blocked even when mounted. The bot's WeCom reply skills always stay available.
rolePermissions.skillsEmpty: No skills installed yet. Install skills from the Skills page to configure them here.
rolePermissions.skillsDisabledHint: Disabled skills are blocked by an explicit deny rule even when mounted.

upgradeBanner.title: Legacy whitelists are disabled
upgradeBanner.body: This bot still has data in the old skill allowlist / bash whitelist fields. Under the new permission model those lists no longer take effect: everyday commands run inside the sandbox with no configuration, and only out-of-sandbox requests need approval. The passlist below starts empty — re-add commands that must run outside the sandbox without approval. Saving this form clears the old data.
